answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring each participant to post a bond whose commitment is folded into a recursive STARK, so identity creation costs scale with the velvet pool rather than being free. A cross-agent bridge contract then emits a signal only when a prover supplies a succinct proof that the folded commitment satisfies the epoch's registration. Correlated defectors incur an exponential capital forfeiture bounded by O(Delta * S).
